title: Three-goal tether: 14d personal KPI check & micro-retro
body:
Purpose:
Short pocket doc to run a lightweight 14-day loop on three personal metrics I want to keep nudging. Not an OKR that cascades to anyone — just an experiment to see if small cadence + clear micro-actions changes throughput and energy.

Three metrics (the tether):
1) Deep work slots landed (target: 8 slots / 14 days)
   - definition: uninterrupted 60–90m blocks focused on a single priority (no Slack, no GitHub notifications, airplane mode on phone).
   - measurement: calendar blocks tagged "DW"; count number of completed blocks (not just scheduled).

2) PRs merged that unblock others (target: 6 PRs / 14 days)
   - definition: PRs where at least one reviewer was blocked on my change or that remove a cross-team dependency.
   - measurement: manual tally in this doc + quick note in PR description: "meets: unblock-count"

3) Restorative mornings (target: 9 / 14 days)
   - definition: first 90 minutes after waking without work inbox; includes 20m movement and 15m reading or planning.
   - measurement: morning checkbox in daily note; count only if >80% of routine completed.

Weekly check-in template (use on days 7 and 14):
- Date:
- Deep work slots completed this period: X / 8 → quick note on what helped/hurt.
- Unblock PRs merged: Y / 6 → which ones had best impact?
- Restorative mornings: Z / 9 → energy delta?
- One surprising win: short sentence.
- Biggest friction: short sentence.
- Hypothesis for next 14d (one-sentence change).
- 3 micro-actions to try next period (<= 15m each).

Micro-retro prompts (quick, honest):
- What did I actually enjoy this period?
- Where did I waste the most time?
- Which habit felt too brittle? (why?)
- What would have doubled impact if I did/do it consistently?
- Immediate removal: what should I stop doing next period?

Observed patterns (notes from current 14d run):
- Week 1: pushed deep work but kept getting pulled into async meetings mid-block → need clearer calendar boundaries.
- PR pattern: quick fixes get merged fast but larger diffs stall without a reviewer ping; reviewers often react to a Slack bump.
- Mornings: when I plan the day the night before, mornings are calm; when I don’t, I check email first and the day fragments.

Decisions & tiny experiments to run next 14d:
1) Calendar gating: put "Focus - do not disturb" event for the first deep slot; create a "soft buffer" 15m after meetings to avoid instant context switching.
2) PR unblocking ritual: allocate one 30m slot every other day explicitly for writing short PR descriptions and nudging reviewers (one-sentence ping + reviewer tag).
3) Morning anchor tweak: move phone to another room and prep a 5-line plan the night before.

Success criteria for this experiment (end of 14d):
- Deep work >= 8 AND at least 50% of those were 75+ minutes without interruption.
- PRs merged >= 6 with at least 2 tagged as "unblock" in reviewers' threads.
- Restorative mornings >= 9 and subjective energy +1 on a 5pt scale on average.

Backlog (next actions if success/fail):
- If success: standardize the gating event and add a recurring PR ritual; share notes with team (short Slack thread).
- If fail due to meetings: propose a meeting-free deep day once/week for the next month and measure impact.
- If fail due to mornings: try a 21-day bedtime anchor before repeating metrics.

Notes to self (messy):
- Be ok with sliding numbers; focus on directional improvement.
- Tiny wins compound: one extra deep block a week is a big deal over a quarter.
- Keep the measurement cheap — manual counts are fine here.

Unresolved questions:
- Is 60–90m the right length for my tasks or should I try 45+45 split? (A/B in next period?)
- Can I delegate one recurring meeting that eats my prime slots? Who to ask?

Quick wins to do today:
- Block two DW slots for next 5 working days and label "DW".
- Add "unblock" tag to current open PRs where appropriate and ping reviewers with a one-line context.
- Prepare a one-sentence plan for tomorrow night.

End note: keep this lightweight — I want this doc to be a nudging mechanism, not another daily ritual that becomes bureaucratic. Re-check on 2026-03-09 (14 days after start).
